optional_codes.reason: Hydrochlorothiazide is taken for hypertension, a chronic condition, so the long-term drug therapy code is supportable. The note does not state that it has been taken for an extended period, so the code is not required. Either answer is defensible.

citations.case: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines FY2027, Section IV.G (list first the diagnosis chiefly responsible for the services provided; list additional codes for coexisting conditions); Section IV.J (code all documented conditions that coexist at the time of the visit and that require or affect patient care, treatment or management); Section I.B.13 (laterality: the code names the side documented); Section I.B.5 (signs and symptoms associated routinely with a disease process are not assigned as additional codes); Section I.C.21.c.3 (category Z79 is assigned when a medication is taken for an extended period as treatment of a chronic condition)

coder_notes: Cellulitis is documented in the right lower leg only. The left leg is normal apart from a healed scar from 2019, which is incidental and not coded. Hypertension is documented and was managed at this visit (medication continued), so it is reported as a coexisting condition. The long-term drug therapy code for hydrochlorothiazide is accepted but not required, because the note does not say how long the medication has been taken (see optional_codes). Fever and the raised white cell count are attributed to the cellulitis and are not coded separately. Sepsis is not documented. There is no abscess, ulcer or open wound. Traps: the left-leg code (L03.116) because the left shin is mentioned; an unspecified-side or bilateral code; coding fever or the white cell count; assigning sepsis from the vital signs and white cell count
